Build the cluster layer: typed, many-to-many families of EINs

Source: R/md-clusters.R
md_build_clusters.Rd

Writes cluster (one row per cluster), cluster_member (one row per cluster and EIN) and cluster_footprint (members per cluster, layer and state). An EIN can belong to many clusters, of different types. A chapter that is hard to match on its own can then be matched one level up: a query whose name matches one member and whose address matches another is still a strong match to the cluster.

Usage

md_build_clusters(
  con = NULL,
  types = c("group_exemption", "related_system", "care_of_network", "shared_website",
    "brand", "co_tenant"),
  max_cotenants = 3L,
  max_website = 5000L,
  brand_min_share = 0.5,
  brand_min_eins = 10L,
  brand_alone_share = 0.8
)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

types

Which cluster types to build.

max_cotenants

Largest shared place that still counts as co-tenancy.

max_website

Largest website key that still forms a cluster.

brand_min_share, brand_min_eins

The brand-word thresholds above.

brand_alone_share

An anchor this concentrated needs no second word of the brand name to make an EIN a member.

Value

Clusters and memberships per type, invisibly.

Cluster types

group_exemption (GRP-)

the components of entity_group - see md_build_groups(). Central is group_central_ein.

related_system (SYS-)

one cluster per Schedule R discloser: the filer and every related or disregarded entity it lists that is in entity. A star, never a connected component: chained together these edges form one component of 117,869 EINs across the health and university sectors. Overlapping stars are kept as they are.

care_of_network (ICO-)

one cluster per organisation named in other EINs' in-care-of field. Only values that read as an organisation are used: not a person (census first name and surname), not a role (TREASURER), not an agent (bank, trust company, CPA, law firm); naming exactly one EIN's legal or dba name, of two or more words, in the same state. Needs the peopleparser census name table.

shared_website (WEB-)

one cluster per website key held by two or more EINs (at most max_website). A national body's site written by its chapters.

brand (BRD-)

one cluster per brand word: a name word that is concentrated in one name, the way TOASTMASTERS is, rather than spread across many, the way BAPTIST is. A word is a brand when one full name holds at least brand_min_share of the EINs carrying the word, and that name is held by at least brand_min_eins EINs. Each dominant name gives one brand, anchored on its most concentrated word: LIONS, not CLUBS; AMATEUR, not STATES. A first pass let every word of a dominant name be its own brand, and STATES gathered 42,951 EINs. Members are every EIN whose legal or dba name contains the anchor word. This is what reaches the 63% of Toastmasters clubs that are in no group exemption.

co_tenant (CTN-)

one cluster per street address shared by 2 to max_cotenants EINs: a school and its PTO, a hospital and its foundation. Larger shared places are registered agents and processing centres, which say nothing about affiliation.

Columns

cluster: cluster_id, cluster_type, central_ein (NULL where the type has none), size, label (the central EIN's legal name, or the shared key) and brand_tokens (name words held by at least half the members, for clusters of three or more).

cluster_member: cluster_id, ein, role (central, parent, intermediate or member) and evidence.

cluster_footprint: cluster_id, layer, state, n_eins. Layers partition EINs, so the footprint of any selection of layers is the exact sum of its rows - the same rule as ein_key_layer.

What this does not do

It does not nest clusters into levels (chapter, state body, national), and it does not merge overlapping clusters. Both are left to the consumer, which can see every membership.
